Application Materials.content:
For the application you will need:
- Transcripts and certificates of any essential qualifications.
- Referee details.
- A personal statement, if applicable to your chosen course.
- Your Queen’s student ID if you are a current / former student.
**If you have completed your qualification, you should upload your degree award certificate and degree transcript. If you have not yet completed your degree, please upload your transcript to show results to date.**
For International Applicants: to make sure your application is processed in the fastest possible time, you must scan and upload the following supporting documents along with your application. The University may not be able to make a decision until all relevant documents have been received:
- Degree transcripts for all completed periods of study (undergraduate level and above).
- If your degree is still in progress, a transcript of results achieved to date.
- Copies of official Degree/Diploma Certificates for qualification(s) already completed.
- Certified translations if original documents are not in English.
- Evidence of an acceptable level of competency in the English language, if your first language is not English.
For all applications (Postgraduate Taught and Research), you must include the names and contact details of **two referees**, normally academics familiar with your undergraduate and/or postgraduate studies. If you have taken a higher degree or postgraduate course recently, one referee should be from that institution. If you have been away from higher education for some time, you may use an employer as one referee. You do not need to include reference letters with your application; these will be requested directly by the University if required.

Application Deadlines.content: Applicants are advised to apply as early as possible and ideally no later than **14th August 2026** for courses which commence in **late September**. In the event that any programme receives a high number of applications, the University reserves the right to close the application portal prior to the deadline stated on course finder.

Academic Requirements.content:
Normally a **2.2 Honours degree (with a minimum of 55%)** or equivalent qualification acceptable to the University in a discipline with relevant quantitative modules. Performance in these relevant quantitative modules should be of the required standard. Applicants with a 2.2 Honours degree (scoring below 55%) or equivalent qualification acceptable to the University and sufficient relevant experience will be considered on a case-by-case basis.
Relevant quantitative modules could include: Finance/Economics/Business school courses, or subjects such as Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, Science, Analytics, Operations Research, Information Technology, Computer Science, Data Management, Information Systems, Actuarial Studies, or Management Science.
For applicants from China Mainland: applicants should hold a good four-year bachelor degree from a recognised, well ranked university with an average grade of at least 70-85%. For the **UK 2.2 Hons with 55% standard** applicable to this programme:
| Type of institution | UK 2.2 Hons with 55% standard |
| --- | --- |
| Tier 1 | Final average **72.5%** |
| Tier 2 | Final average **77.5%** |
| Tier 3 | Final average **82.5%** |
**Tier 1:** Prestigious Universities (Double First Class Universities and Top 100 Academic Ranking of World Universities). **Tier 2:** Other Recognised Universities and Independent Colleges affiliated to a Tier 1 Institution (as defined by Queen's). **Tier 3:** Other Independent Colleges recognised by Ministry of Education and Self-Study Degrees.
For China Mainland borderline cases: where entry requirements are different, borderline cases will be considered at the discretion of the Academic Selector. Sometimes, it may be possible to exercise flexibility when applicants have fallen more than 2% below the target grade when final results are known; the decision will be at the discretion of the Academic Selector.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Evidence of an **IELTS score of 6.5, with not less than 5.5 in any component**, or an equivalent qualification acceptable to the University is required. IELTS must be **taken within the last 2 years**.
International students wishing to apply to Queen's University Belfast, and for whom English is not their first language, must be able to demonstrate their proficiency in English. Non-EEA nationals must also satisfy UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) immigration requirements for English language for visa purposes. More information: [www.qub.ac.uk/EnglishLanguageReqs](https://www.qub.ac.uk/EnglishLanguageReqs).
If you need to improve your English language skills before entering this degree programme, [Queen's University Belfast International Study Centre](https://qubisc.com/en?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/financial-analytics-msc/&utm_term=INTO+Queen%27s+University+Belfast) offers English language courses, including:
- [Academic English](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/academic-english?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/financial-analytics-msc/&utm_term=Academic+English): an intensive English language and study skills course for successful university study at degree level.
- [Pre-sessional English](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/financial-analytics-msc/&utm_term=Pre-sessional+English): a short intensive academic English course for students starting a degree programme at Queen's University Belfast and who need to improve their English.

Program Overview.content:
The MSc Financial Analytics is for students with an interest in financial markets or financial technology (FinTech) who enjoy working with data. It shows how data science, analytics, statistics and programming tools are used in the real world for the analysis and modelling of financial and economic data. The programme equips students with cutting-edge quantitative and computational techniques utilised by industry leading firms, bridging the gap between complex quantitative models and financial decision making by developing dual skillsets in both finance and data analysis.
Attendance is 1 year full-time, and the course location is Queen's Business School. The degree can lead to careers in areas such as financial data science, trading, software development, portfolio management, consulting, data analytics, risk management, business analytics and academia.
Queen’s University is ranked third in the UK for Graduate Prospects in Accounting and Finance (Times and Sunday Times Good University Guide 2024).
Professional accreditations and partnerships:
- The programme has been accepted into the CFA Institute University Recognition Program and aligns with the Candidate Body of Knowledge (CBOK), the core knowledge, skills, and abilities generally accepted and applied by investment professionals worldwide.
- Queen’s Business School is an academic partner of the Certificate in Quantitative Finance (CQF) Institute. Through this partnership, MSc Financial Analytics students benefit from access to CQF Institute resources including industry talks and workshops, research, networking opportunities and career tools.
Facilities and student experience:
- Many classes are held in the state-of-the-art FinTrU Trading Room, which provides access to Bloomberg software used by many leading financial institutions worldwide.
- Students also have exposure to S&P Capital IQ and learn in-demand programming and data science skills such as Python, R, SQL, Hadoop, Spark, Google Cloud, and Posit Workbench, an Azure-based enterprise grade data science platform.
- Students are strongly encouraged to join the Student Managed Fund, where they have an opportunity to manage real money.
Course structure:
- This degree equips students with cutting-edge quantitative and computational techniques used by leading finance and FinTech firms and prepares them for careers in quantitative finance, trading, portfolio management, data analytics or risk management.
- Students learn how data science, business analytics, programming and statistical tools are used for the analysis and modelling of complex financial data.
- In Semester 3, students complete either an Academic Dissertation, described as a thesis-based research project motivated by contemporary quantitative academic research with supervision from an academic expert in the chosen area, or an Applied Research Project, an industry-focused module with a taught component at the start of the summer and a final report in the form of an in-depth equity analyst report of a CFA standard.
People teaching you:
- [Dr Fearghal Kearney](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/fearghal-kearney), Programme Director, Finance. Email: F.Kearney@qub.ac.uk
Learning and teaching:
- The programme equips students with cutting-edge quantitative and computational analytical skills demanded by leading firms worldwide and prepares them for future careers in quantitative finance, trading, more general finance, FinTech and business consulting environments.
- The course bridges the gap between quantitative models and financial decision-making, with many modules focusing on learning through simulation.
Career prospects:
- This programme equips students with quantitative and computational techniques and strategies used by leading finance and financial technology firms.
- Full-service finance and business consulting firms employ Financial Analytics professionals, as do boutique firms such as asset managers and hedge funds. IT software organisations are also attracted to graduates from this programme because of their specialism at the interface between computing, data analytics and finance.
- Graduate prospects from the MSc Financial Analytics are described as excellent; Queen’s was ranked first in the UK for Graduate Prospects in Accounting and Finance (Times and Sunday Times Good University Guide 2023).
- Graduates have secured roles with employers such as Citi, Deutsche Bank, Bank of China, Davy Group, Citco, Amazon, FD Technologies, Data Intellect and many others.
- Typical roles include data scientists, financial engineers, software developers, equity analysts, consultants, portfolio analysts, risk analysts, business analysts, and traders.

Curriculum.content:
Attendance: **1 year (Full-time)**.
Course Structure: This degree will equip students with cutting-edge quantitative and computational techniques. Students learn how data science, business analytics, programming and statistical tools are used for the analysis and modelling of complex financial data.
- **Semester 1:** Asset Pricing; Corporate Finance (optional); Financial Market Structure (optional); Data Management; Financial Data Analytics.
- **Semester 2:** Advanced Analytics and Machine Learning; Financial Modelling in Python; Advanced Financial Data Analytics; AI & Trading.
- **Semester 3:** Academic Dissertation, a thesis-based research project motivated by contemporary quantitative academic research, with supervision provided by an academic with expertise in the chosen area; or Applied Research Project, an industry-focused module with a taught component at the start of the summer and a final report that is an in-depth equity analyst report of a CFA standard.
Modules are subject to change. The module details reflect the current year of study (2025/26).

Financial Aid.content:
**Scholarships of £6000 available exclusively for outstanding international applicants studying postgraduate taught programmes at Queen’s Business School in the academic year 2026/27.** To qualify, applicants must hold an offer to study a postgraduate taught programme at Queen’s Business School. No application necessary; if eligible, confirmation of the award will be issued with the offer.
- The **Queen’s Business School Scholarship** is available only to new students who hold an offer for a place on a **full-time postgraduate taught programme at the Queen’s Business School**, starting in the academic year 2026/27, and who have met any academic and language conditions attached to their offer before commencement of study.
- Students must be classified as international fee-paying students paying the full international tuition fee rate. Students paying NI, ROI, EU or GB fees are not eligible.
- The discount is awarded for the first year of study only and is deducted from **gross** tuition fees upon enrolment.
- Students must be self-funded, i.e. tuition fees are being paid by the student or their parents at the full international tuition fee rate.
- Students receiving funding from an external sponsorship body such as Government, a charity or a private organisation are not eligible for the Queen’s Business School Scholarship 2026/27; this excludes students in receipt of educational loans.
- International scholarships cannot be used in conjunction with any other University tuition fee scholarship, although eligible students can use their scholarship with the Early Confirmation Award or the ISC Scholarship.
- The University is unable to consider requests for increased and/or further funding. The amount of scholarship offered is non-negotiable.
[Terms and Conditions](https://www.qub.ac.uk/Study/international-students/international-scholarships/terms-and-conditions/)

Multiple Applications.content:
After you have entered the core details about yourself and your academic background, you can apply for **one or multiple courses** through the [Queen's Portal](https://go.qub.ac.uk/pgapply).
If you have applied for and been offered a place on more than one programme of study, you must indicate whether you wish to accept or decline the offer against each programme. Given that your final programme choice may be dependent on funding and/or other factors, you may initially decide to accept more than one offer of a place.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: Applications for deferred entry may be permitted. However, in considering requests for deferred entry it will be necessary to consider if the course will be offered in a subsequent year or, in the case of research, the research project and/or intended supervisor is available in a subsequent year. Requests will be considered on an individual basis, particularly in relation to non-UK/Irish applicants who may have experienced delays in obtaining an entry visa in time to commence their studies. Applications for deferral of University administered funding are not permitted.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
- If students need to improve English language skills before entering the MSc Financial Analytics degree programme, [Queen's University Belfast International Study Centre](https://qubisc.com/en?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/financial-analytics-msc/&utm_term=INTO+Queen%27s+University+Belfast) offers English language courses designed to improve English ability for admission to this degree, including [Academic English](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/academic-english?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/financial-analytics-msc/&utm_term=Academic+English) and [Pre-sessional English](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/financial-analytics-msc/&utm_term=Pre-sessional+English), "a short intensive academic English course for students starting a degree programme at Queen's University Belfast and who need to improve their English."
- For international applicants, the mandatory tuition fee deposit is **£1000 International (Non-EU & EU except ROI)**; "this condition of offer is in addition to any academic or English language requirements."
